cells.tense: You are shining right now because the cultivation finished, and nobody had to be watching.
cells.ask: At your next meeting, say the whole pattern out loud before you propose any step, then let the room take it.
cells.core:
You see the whole shape of a thing, and it makes you shine, and the shine is just what seeing looks like from outside. Clean, this runs without effort: you put the pattern on the table and leave it there. You're not selling it and not steering anyone toward it, and the room picks it up on its own. The confidence is real and it was earned, which is why people follow where you're already headed.

Nothing here is being forced. You laid the groundwork, the thing arrived at its own size, and you belong at the front of it without pushing. A next start is already lifting its head, so give it the same treatment: one place, one small beginning, offered to somebody who didn't ask. Same fire, smaller stakes, kept lit past the meeting.
cells.sheetLine: You shine because the thing ripened, not because you pushed.
cells.verb: trust the spark that starts the fire

cells.tense: You are lighting a fire for a room you haven't stepped into yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've already said and don't say it again this week. Wait for somebody to bring it back.
cells.core:
You're already living in the finished version. The thing hasn't happened, but you're talking as if it has — laying out the whole picture, lighting up the people in front of you, certain of a shape that's still only yours. It feels like momentum. Some of it is bracing against a future you can't write in.

Done well, this is the pattern doing the pulling, and you letting the room read it at its own pace. Right now you're arranging the room around the pattern, and the arranging is costing you the view. Let one start be smaller than your enthusiasm for it. Somebody else may carry it somewhere you couldn't have. That's the fire doing its job.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that's already behind you, not through it.
cells.ask: Water one small thing today — a plant, a person's idea, a task somebody started. Ask what it needs.
cells.core:
You can still see the whole pattern — that part works fine. Starting the fire is what stopped, so you keep reading the shape of things instead of walking into one. At its best this was one motion: the sight landed and the hand moved in the same breath. Now the sight is clean, the hand is still, and that gap is the whole trouble.

Tend one small living thing today and nothing more. Not your plan — somebody else's, or a plant's, or a task that's already half-grown. You're not being asked to be radiant. Just to stand next to something that's actually happening and stay long enough to watch it move.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see the pattern — starting it stopped being possible.

cells.tense: You are already writing this thing and calling it the room's handwriting.
cells.ask: Tell whoever is standing closest one choice that was yours. Name the choice, say you made it, and leave it.
cells.core:
The fire is lit. You lit it — in what you started, what you said yes to, what you keep moving. But when it comes up you describe it as the project, the team, the moment. The hand is working and the name isn't on it. At its best this is somebody who knows which moves were theirs and says so without making a speech of it.

Say one choice belongs to you and let that land. Not the whole story, not credit — just one thing you'd quietly filed under circumstances. You don't have to become someone who announces what they do. Say that the hand doing this is yours, then go on doing what it does.
